Rashtriya Raksha University Launches Master’s in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) Programme Cohort 2.0 in Collaboration with Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs
articles.full_content:
Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, engaged with the media in Bengaluru to highlight the second cohort of its flagship Masters in Financial and Economic Security (MFES) programme, a specialised hybrid programme for working professionals, offered in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India.
The MFES Cohort 2.0 marks a significant step forward in RRU’s endeavour to build a specialised professional ecosystem equipped with the knowledge, investigative capabilities and security-oriented understanding required to address the increasingly sophisticated nature of financial and economic crimes in an evolving digital and interconnected financial landscape.
The programme adopts a multidisciplinary and practice-oriented approach, integrating law, finance, investigation, regulation, emerging technologies and economic security through real-world case studies, analytical tools and expert-led learning. The hybrid learning model enables working professionals to balance advanced education with professional commitments while fostering meaningful engagement with experts and networks across law enforcement, regulatory agencies, financial institutions, corporate organisations and the wider RRU–IICA ecosystem.
Speaking about the programme, Prof. (Dr.) Bimal N. Patel, Vice Chancellor, Rashtriya Raksha University, remarked “Financial and economic security is no longer a specialised concern limited to financial institutions; it is increasingly integral to national security, economic resilience and public trust.” He further emphasised that MFES reflects RRU’s vision of connecting learning with purpose, by developing skilled practitioners who can understand emerging threats, respond with expertise and contribute to safeguarding financial integrity.
Mr. Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General and CEO, Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs, stated, “The Masters in Financial and Economic Security is a flagship collaboration between IICA and RRU, created to respond to the evolving challenges of financial and economic crimes. Through advanced analytical tools, legal expertise, investigative techniques and practical learning, the programme seeks to build future leaders equipped to safeguard economic integrity and contribute to a more secure and prosperous future.”
With the launch of MFES Cohort 2.0, RRU and IICA reaffirm their commitment to strengthening India’s pool of specialized workforce in financial and economic security and nurturing skilled practitioners who can anticipate emerging risks, respond effectively and contribute to a secure, resilient and transparent economic environment

Historic Turnout Marks West Bengal’s First-Ever Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat hosted by Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
articles.full_content:
Over 4500 youth shortlisted and more than 7500 interviews conducted
Drawing enthusiastic participation from thousands of aspiring youths, the Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat emerged as a major platform connecting job seekers from Dakshin Dinajpur and neighbouring regions with employment opportunities. Organized by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India in collaboration with the Government of West Bengal and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), the Mahotsav witnessed a historic turnout with over 7500 interviews being conducted. More than 7,000 job opportunities from over 50+ employers provided diverse opportunities to the local youth aspiring to build their careers in different sectors, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, healthcare, hospitality, food processing, banking and financial services, and other services.
The event was attended by Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Minister of State for Education and Minister of State for Development of Northeastern Region, Government of India; Shri Kshudiram Tudu, Minister – In – Charge, Tribal Development Department, Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Joyel Murmu, Minister of State, Irrigation and waterways department and Tribal Development Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Khagen Murmu, Member of Parliament for Malda North; Shri Bidyut Kumar Roy, Member of Legislative Assembly, Balurghat; Shri Badurai Tudu, Member of Legislative Assembly, Tapan; Shri Satyendranath Roy, Member of Legislative Assembly, Gangarampur; Shri Rajiv Kumar, Principal Secretary, Technical Education, Training and Skill Development, Government of West Bengal; Shri VS Arvind, Director, MSDE; Shri Balasubramanium T., District Magistrate, Dakshin Dinajpur; and Shri Abhishek Gupta, Superintendent of Police, Dakshin Dinajpur.
Highlighting that education and skills serve as twin pillars of employability and success, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Minister of State for Education and Minister of State for Development of Northeastern Region, Government of India, said, “the Skill India Mission was envisioned by our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi to ensure the youth of India are skilled and are provided a platform to connect with gainful employment opportunities and Kaushal Mahotsav is one such initiative under his guidance.”
Encouraging productive use of technology, he urged them to harness digital platforms and transform their mobile phones into gateways for learning and growth rather than mere sources of entertainment, calling upon the youth to adopt a culture of lifelong learning and skill development.
He further lauded the efforts of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, for organizing the Kaushal Mahotsav in Balurghat. MSME DFO Dimapur organize PM Vishwakarma One-Day Awareness Workshop on Branding and Marketing in Wokha
articles.full_content:
The MSME Development and Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Dimapur, under the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, in association with the Department of Industries and Commerce and the District Industries Centre (DIC), Wokha, organized a one-day awareness workshop on Branding and Marketing at the DC Conference Hall, Wokha on August 18, 2026, under the PM Vishwakarma scheme.
The workshop aimed to strengthen the entrepreneurial capabilities of PM Vishwakarma artisans by providing practical knowledge on product packaging, labelling and design, business development, export development, Artificial Intelligence (AI), e-commerce, QR code generation and financial literacy. Over 97 artisans, including tailors, carpenters, barbers and basket makers, participated in the programme from across the district.
The programme commenced with a welcome address delivered by Shri K. Myingthungo Kikon, General Manager, DIC Wokha. The keynote address was delivered by Shri K. Mathung Tsanglao, NCS, Deputy Commissioner of Wokha, who addressed participants and highlighted the workshop's vital role in empowering local artisans. He emphasized the importance of building market knowledge and leveraging e-commerce platforms, encouraging artisans to embrace modern marketing approaches to boost their visibility, reach wider customer bases, and grow their businesses. During the event, under his chairmanship, loan sanctions were officially announced for two artisans—a basket maker and a carpenter—under the Central Bank of India, Wokha Branch.
The first technical session on Product Packaging, Labelling and Design was delivered by Smt. Therali Ovung, Proprietor, The Sewist Design Studio and Training Centre, Wokha. The session focused on product development based on customer needs and market demand, highlighting the importance of effective packaging, labelling, product design, and branding.
An interactive session on Business Development was conducted by Smt. Bwenye Kemp, Financial Analyst, RAMP. The session covered business planning, SMART targets, networking, digital business development, identifying product strengths and Unique Selling Propositions (USP), understanding target customers and appropriate pricing strategies.
The Artificial Intelligence and E-commerce Onboarding session was conducted by the State Programme Management Unit (SPMU), PM Vishwakarma wherein the participants were introduced to emerging digital technologies and their applications in product promotion, marketing and enterprise development.
The session on Export Development was conducted by Shri Mhachan N. Kikon, Functional Manager, DIC Wokha, who provided insights into export readiness, accessing international markets and available Government support schemes. The QR Code Generation session was conducted by Smt. Ronbeni C. Lotha, Executive, India Post Payments Bank, Wokha Branch, who highlighted DBT account opening and its benefits under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.

Senior Officers from BRICS Member Countries hold discussions on Key Priorities of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development in New Delhi
articles.full_content:
Under India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, Senior Officers’ Meeting of the Environment Working Group and Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development was held in Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 17th August 2026. The meeting was chaired by Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, Shri Tanmay Kumar. The proceedings witnessed participation from BRICS member countries including Federative Republic of Brazil, People’s Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Indonesia, Islamic Republic of Iran, Russian Federation, Republic of South Africa and United Arab Emirates.
Secretary, @moefcc , Shri Tanmay Kumar, welcomed the distinguished delegates from BRICS Member Countries to the Environment Working Group-Senior Officers' Meeting affirming solidarity & shared commitments towards a sustainable future. #BRICS2026 #BRICSIndia2026 … pic.twitter.com/6T5n3bWabA
In his keynote address, the Chair stated that over the past two decades, the BRICS alliance has expanded from an economic dialogue into an increasingly influential platform for defining its approach to the critical challenges facing the environment, including pressing global issues of increasing pollution, biodiversity loss as well as global warming. He said, "Our partnership has broadened in terms of relevance to sustainable development, climate resilience and adaptation, resource efficiency and circular economy, as well as environmental governance."
The Chair informed that BRICS 2026 has been guided by the vision of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, that global cooperation must remain people-centric by advancing a humanity-first approach. This vision finds expression in the Chairship theme - 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability'. India has sought to advance environmental action through approaches that integrate ecological sustainability with development objectives, it was stated.
Over the course of India’s Chairship, the Environment Working Group and the Contact Group on Climate Change and Sustainable Development have together advanced cooperation across four interconnected priority areas: Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles; Afforestation, Forest Fire Management and Disaster Resilience; Circular Economy and Adaptation.
The Chair stated that these priorities reflect both the shared environmental challenges confronting the BRICS countries and the collective wisdom and strength to address them. They reflect the unanimous recognition that climate resilience, ecosystem restoration, resource efficiency and sustainable development are deeply interconnected challenges that require integrated and holistic responses rather than isolated interventions in silos.

The meeting was chaired by Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, Shri Tanmay Kumar. The proceedings witnessed participation from BRICS member countries including Federative Republic of Brazil, People’s Republic of China, Arab Republic of Egypt, Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Republic of Indonesia, Islamic Republic of Iran, Russian Federation, Republic of South Africa and United Arab Emirates.

PRESS NOTE ON PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) MONTHLY BULLETIN July, 2026
articles.full_content:
LFPR improved in both rural and urban areas WPR strengthened in both rural and urban areas UR declined
• Overall LFPR (15 years and above) increased to 55.4% in July 2026, from 54.4% in June 2026.
• Rural LFPR (15 years and above) increased by 1.4 percentage points over the previous month, reaching 58.0% in July 2026.
• Female LFPR (15 years and above) rose to 34.4% in July 2026, registering an increase of 1.7 percentage points over the previous month.
• Overall WPR (15 years and above) increased to 52.5% in July 2026, marking the first increase since February 2026.
• Rural WPR (15 years and above) stood at 55.4% in July 2026, registering an increase of 1.6 percentage points over June 2026 and 1.0 percentage point over July 2025.
• Overall UR (15 years and above) declined to 5.1% in July 2026, lower than both the previous month and the corresponding month of the previous year.
• Both male and female UR (15 years and above) declined in July 2026 compared with the previous month, indicating an improvement in employment conditions across both genders.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to June, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for July, 2026 is the sixteenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
• Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) improved:
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 55.4% in July, 2026, from 54.4% in June, 2026. After declining from March to May, 2026 and remaining unchanged in June, 2026, the overall LFPR increased in July, 2026. The same trend was also observed in rural areas, where the LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above increased to 58.0% in July, 2026, from 56.6% in June, 2026, registering an increase of 1.4 percentage points. In urban areas, LFPR increased marginally, from 50.1% in June, 2026 to 50.4% in July, 2026.
Compared to the same month of the previous year, the overall LFPR increased by 0.5 percentage point, from 54.9% in July, 2025 to 55.4% in July, 2026. During the same period, rural LFPR also increased by 1.1 percentage points, from 56.9% to 58.0%, while urban LFPR experienced a marginal decline by 0.3 percentage point, from 50.7% to 50.4%.
• Rise in female labour force participation:
The overall female LFPR experienced a noticeable increase from 32.7%

MSDE convenes ‘Kaushal Manthan’ Regional Conference of Skill Ministers in Kolkata
articles.full_content:
Shri Jayant Chaudhary calls for transforming ITIs into industry-responsive institutions linked with sustainable careers States deliberate on PM-SETU, decentralised planning, industry partnerships and workforce mobility
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) convened ‘Kaushal Manthan’, the Regional Conference of Skill Ministers in Kolkata today. The Conference brought together Ministers and senior officers from participating States and Union Territory to strengthen Centre–State coordination and advance an industry-connected, outcome-oriented skilling ecosystem.
The Conference was chaired by Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India.
It was attended by Shri Jagannath Chattopadhyay, Minister-in-charge- Higher Education Department and Technical Education, Training and Skill Development Department, Government of West Bengal; Shri Kunvarjibhai Mohanbhai Bavaliya, Minister of Labour, Skill Development and Employment Department, Government of Gujarat; Guru Khushwant Saheb, Minister for Skill Development, Technical Education & Employment and Scheduled Caste Development, Government of Chhattisgarh; Dr. Gotam Tetwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Skill Development and Employment, Government of Madhya Pradesh; Shri Sampad Chandra Swain, Minister of State (Independent Charge) Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education Government of Odisha and Dr HareKrishna Bera, MoS- Technical Education, Training and Skill Development department. Senior representatives from Goa, Jharkhand and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu also participated.
Addressing the Conference, Shri Jayant Chaudhary said, “India’s young people bring extraordinary ambition, adaptability and potential. Our responsibility is to connect that potential with future-ready, industry-valued skills and real opportunities. PM-SETU gives us a historic opportunity to reimagine ITIs as vibrant centres of excellence, innovation and aspiration. Achieving this will require strong convergence between the Centre, States, industry and training institutions, aligning policy, infrastructure and investment around the learner. Its success will ultimately be reflected in the careers, enterprises and upward mobility we enable”.
The Minister emphasised that the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) Scheme should be implemented as a comprehensive institutional reform. He encouraged States to align PM-SETU clusters with priority economic value chains, industrial corridors, MSME concentrations, emerging technologies and upcoming investments, with Spoke ITIs receiving dependable access to Hub laboratories, master trainers, career services and employer networks.

Ministry of MSME Joins Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026 with Enthusiasm; Celebrates 150 Years of Vande Mataram
articles.full_content:
Secretary, Ministry of MSME Distributes Tiranga Among Officials; MSME Ministry Offices Across the Country Join ‘Selfie with Tiranga’ Initiative
The Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026 is being observed from 9th to 17th August 2026 to inspire citizens to display the National Flag at their homes and workplaces and reaffirm their pride in the Tiranga. The campaign also commemorates the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram.”
The Government of India launched the Har Ghar Tiranga (HGT) Campaign in 2022 under the aegis of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav to encourage citizens to hoist the National Flag at their homes and foster a personal connection with the Tiranga. Over the years, the campaign has evolved into a Jan Bhagidari movement, symbolising national identity, patriotism and pride.
In this connection, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises organised a special programme on 13th August 2026 to promote patriotism, national unity and respect for the National Flag. Attached, subordinate and field offices under the Ministry were also encouraged to observe the occasion at their respective workplaces. The programme further highlighted the significance of the 150th anniversary of “Vande Mataram”, reinforcing the spirit of national pride and unity.
As part of the celebrations, the Secretary, Ministry of MSME, distributed the National Flag (Tiranga) among officers and officials and encouraged their active participation in the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign 2026.
The programme also commemorated the 150th anniversary of “Vande Mataram”, which was collectively sung by the officers and staff. Participants were sensitised to the campaign’s objectives and the importance of displaying the National Flag with due dignity and respect.
Officers and staff were also encouraged to participate in the “Selfie with Tiranga” initiative by uploading their photographs on the Har Ghar Tiranga website ( www.harghartiranga.com ) , thereby promoting public participation and collective pride in the Tiranga.
The celebrations reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to fostering patriotism, unity, public participation and respect for the National Flag.

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 3rd Meeting of Apex Monitoring Authority of NICDIT and reviews the progress of projects under NICDP
articles.full_content:
Smt. Sitharaman urges for faster completion of infrastructure, land allotment, investment and commencement of production Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal calls for investor-ready industrial ecosystems with plug-and-play infrastructure Shri Piyush Goyal calls for PM GatiShakti-aligned, integrated area-development approach for BHAVYA and future industrial developments BHAVYA receives strong response from States in 1st round
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, chaired the 3rd Meeting of the Apex Monitoring Authority of the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) in New Delhi today. The meeting reviewed the progress of projects under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) and deliberated on priorities for the next phase of industrial corridor development.
The meeting was attended by Union Minister for Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal; Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav; and Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog, Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri.
Chairing the meeting, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman appreciated the progress made under NICDP and said that the encouraging results on the ground indicate growing investor demand. She emphasised that the next pipeline of industrial land and infrastructure should be prepared well before the existing inventory is exhausted.
Smt. Sitharaman stated that Industrial Corridors are an important pillar of the Government of India’s strategy to expand manufacturing, strengthen logistics competitiveness and create globally competitive industrial ecosystems.
Recalling the emphasis placed at the previous Apex meeting, she said that Industrial Corridor development should be taken forward in the spirit of ‘Team India’. She also underlined the importance of convergence of Freight, Industrial Development, Railways and Expressways, the FIRE Corridors, for the success of the programme.
The Finance Minister stressed that the focus must now move beyond project approvals towards timely completion of infrastructure, land allotment, investment and commencement of production. She urged States to resolve bottlenecks relating to land, connectivity, utilities, statutory clearances and the powers of project Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs).
She further stressed the need for integrated planning through PM GatiShakti and continued use of investor-friendly land allotment mechanisms. Worker housing, healthcare, skilling, public transport and other social amenities, she said, should form an integral part of industrial development.
Smt. Sitharaman also highlighted the Government of India’s support for infrastructure and manufacturing through enhanced public capital expenditure, support to States under SASCI, improved credit support for manufacturing MSMEs, and tax and customs measures aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing and supply chains.
